harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to route between lan-a (10.10.10.0/24, vtnet1/opt1) and lan-b (10.10.20.0/24, vtnet2/opt2), added static IPs and cross routes on node2 (lan-a, 10.10.10.2) and node3 (lan-b, 10.10.20.2), and added firewall rules to block+log TCP/23 between the two networks while allowing other traffic. Verified a telnet (tcp/23) connection attempt from node2 to node3 is refused and logged on node1's filter log. Then executed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time, confirming boot-identity change and post-restart recovery of interfaces, routes, firewall rules, and the block+log behavior for a fresh attempt from node2.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 topology and interfaces
Read node1 /conf/config.xml to understand existing OPNsense config
Configured static IPs and cross-network routes on node2 (10.10.10.2/24) and node3 (10.10.20.2/24) via nmcli
Added opt1 (LAN_A, vtnet1, 10.10.10.1/24) and opt2 (LAN_B, vtnet2, 10.10.20.1/24) interfaces to node1's config.xml and activated them via configctl interface invoke registration + reconfigure
Added OPNsense filter rules: block+log TCP/23 in both directions between opt1 and opt2, plus general pass rules for other traffic; applied via configctl filter reload
Verified ping connectivity between lan-a and lan-b, and that ICMP passes while TCP/23 is blocked
Started a python TCP/23 listener on node3 and attempted a connection from node2, confirming refusal
Located the corresponding refused-attempt log entry in node1's /var/log/filter/*.log
Captured pre-restart boot-identity baselines (kern.boottime on node1, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on node2/node3) and health evidence
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 one at a time using background-scheduled native reboot commands, polling each until exec was available again
Confirmed changed boot identity on each node post-restart

Verified post-restart recovery: interfaces/IPs, static routes, OPNsense filter ruleset (including the block+log telnet rules) persisted, and re-tested the block+log behavior with a fresh telnet attempt from node2 to node3, confirming a new log entry

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
evidence.summary: Added opt1/opt2 interfaces on node1 (10.10.10.1, 10.10.20.1), configured node2/node3 with static IPs and cross routes, and confirmed ping connectivity across the two networks via node1.

evidence.requirement: Refuse TCP port 23 between lan-a and lan-b
evidence.summary: Added block rules for tcp/23 between opt1 and opt2 in config.xml, reloaded pf, and confirmed a live TCP/23 connection attempt from node2 to node3 timed out (refused) while a general pass rule still allows other traffic.

evidence.requirement: Record every refused attempt in a log on node1
evidence.summary: Block rules configured with <log>1</log>; node1's /var/log/filter/filter_*.log shows block entries with the matching rule label for tcp/23 traffic 10.10.10.2->10.10.20.2 port 23.

evidence.requirement: Show a log entry produced by an attempt made from node2
evidence.summary: Node2 initiated a TCP/23 connect to node3 (10.10.20.2), which timed out; node1's filter log line with sequenceId 209-211 shows block,in,vtnet1,tcp,10.10.10.2,10.10.20.2,...,23 matching that exact attempt.

Captured baseline kern.boottime (16:24:13), issued a background reboot, observed SSH connection timeout confirming disconnection, polled until reachable again with kern.boottime changed to 16:29:05, then verified interfaces, firewall rules, and block+log behavior all recovered with a fresh logged refusal from node2.

Captured baseline boot_id (d6298ced...), triggered systemctl reboot, observed connection timeout, polled until reachable with new boot_id (086ac571...), and verified static IP/route/connectivity to node1 recovered.

Captured baseline boot_id (5fb1b173...), triggered systemctl reboot, observed connection timeout, polled until reachable with new boot_id (8e43826c...), and verified static IP/route/connectivity to node1 recovered.
